title: English Vocabulary 4 · Units 25–26
description: Advanced travel vocabulary for motoring law, traffic incidents, fare conditions, transport, accommodation and holiday expressions.
sourceNotice: Prepared for personal study from the user-provided textbook. Vocabulary learning targets are grounded in the assigned teaching pages, exercises and answer key; Portuguese translations, example sentences and usage notes are independently written. Original exercises and extended source passages are not reproduced.

audit.scope: Units 25–26, both teaching pages and facing exercises, the transport choices diagram, term definitions, register notes, exercises 25.1–25.3 and 26.1–26.4, and corresponding answer key.
audit.pronunciation: Broad British IPA is given selectively for shorter terms where confident; unverified or longer multi-word expressions use blank ipa rather than guesswork. Accent variants and connected speech are not exhaustively represented.
audit.languagePolicy: All learner-facing text is English except natural Brazilian Portuguese inside pt.
audit.reviewMethod: Compared the source teaching pages, layout, diagrams and exercises with the book answer key. Wrote original examples and notes. Checked package schema, identifiers, per-item fields, provenance, pronunciation-target hygiene and JSON readability by script. Browser import, browser TTS and speech recognition were not tested.
audit.limitations: No bundled MP3 audio. Browser and live VocabLab app tests were not performed. The source uses UK driving conventions; traffic rules, penalties, insurance and accommodation terms may differ by country.

units.title: Unit 25 — On the road: traffic and driving
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 25. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
units.category: Travel and transport · driving regulations, offences and road disruption
learningObjectives: Use precise British-English terms for traffic regulations, right of way, vehicle safety and driving offences.
Describe congestion, accidents and unexpected road restrictions with natural collocations.
Distinguish formal motoring terms from informal spoken expressions such as conk out and back-seat driver.
Recognise legal and regional variation in road terminology without assuming that all rules are universal.

items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: Drivers must give way to cyclists when the signs require it.
items.note: Often give way to somebody or something; UK road-sign terminology, not the same as stop.

items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: Slow down when you approach the give-way sign.
items.note: A sign indicating that other traffic has priority; a full stop may not always be required.

items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: Take the second exit at the roundabout.
items.note: A circular road junction; priority rules vary by country.

items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: At this junction, the buses have right of way.
items.note: The priority to go before other road users; common in have the right of way.

items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: The new pedestrian crossing is close to the primary school.
items.note: In Britain a zebra crossing is a particular kind of pedestrian crossing.

items.pt: faixa de pedestres com listras brancas
items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: A driver stopped at the zebra crossing to let us cross.
items.note: A marked crossing, especially in British English; local priority rules vary.

items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: She sounded her horn to warn the other driver.
items.note: More formal than beep your horn; sound here means make the horn produce a noise.

items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: Please do not beep your horn outside the hospital.
items.note: Less formal alternative to sound your horn.

items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: Parking is prohibited outside the emergency entrance.
items.note: Formal wording for something forbidden by rules or law; often followed by in or from.

items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: The camera recorded a van jumping a red light.
items.note: British idiom for passing a traffic signal while it is red; US English also uses run a red light.

items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: The prosecutor argued that the driver had engaged in reckless driving.
items.note: Driving with serious disregard for safety; legal categories vary across jurisdictions.

items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: Driving dangerously can be a serious offence.
items.note: Offence is British spelling; American English offense.

items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: The council launched a campaign against drink-driving.
items.note: British-English noun for driving after consuming too much alcohol; US: drunk driving.

items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: The new rules include penalties for drug-driving.
items.note: Driving while impaired by drugs; not necessarily the same offence as drink-driving.

items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: The officer asked the motorist to take a breathalyser test.
items.note: Breathalyser is a common British spelling for an alcohol breath-testing device.

items.pt: acidente com fuga do local; acidente em que o responsável foge
items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: Police appealed for witnesses to a hit-and-run accident.
items.note: The driver involved leaves without stopping; also used as hit-and-run as a modifier.

items.pt: proibição de dirigir; suspensão do direito de dirigir
items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: The court imposed a two-year driving ban.
items.note: Legal restriction on driving; the exact measure depends on national law.

items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: The maximum penalty may include imprisonment.
items.note: Formal legal noun; distinguish imprisonment as a penalty from an ordinary fine.

items.pt: pontos na carteira de motorista por infrações
items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: Repeated traffic offences can lead to penalty points.
items.note: British licensing system; points may accumulate and lead to a driving ban.

items.pt: multa aplicada no local da infração
items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: She received an on-the-spot fine for parking illegally.
items.note: Issued at the scene of an offence; do not confuse with a fine paid immediately.

items.pt: direção sem o devido cuidado; condução negligente
items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: The driver was cited for careless driving after the incident.
items.note: British legal description; meaning and threshold differ from reckless driving.

items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: The inspection checks whether exhaust emissions meet the required limit.
items.note: Gases released by an engine; exhaust is pronounced /ɪɡˈzɔːst/.

items.pt: em condições seguras e legais de circulação
items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: The mechanic confirmed that the vehicle was roadworthy.
items.note: Describes a vehicle fit and safe to be used on the road.

items.pt: sulcos da banda de rodagem do pneu
items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: The inspector measured the tyre tread before approving the car.
items.note: Tread is the patterned outer surface of a tyre; tyre is British spelling, US tire.

items.pt: pneu careca; pneu com banda de rodagem desgastada
items.section: A · Driving regulations and road users
items.example: The garage replaced a bald tyre before our journey.
items.note: A tyre whose tread is worn away; a safety hazard.

items.section: B · Traffic problems and road incidents
items.example: The ring road is often gridlocked during rush hour.
items.note: Period of the day when commuter traffic is heaviest.

items.pt: fila longa de veículos parados ou lentos
items.section: B · Traffic problems and road incidents
items.example: A broken-down lorry caused a long tailback on the motorway.
items.note: Mainly British English for a queue of slow-moving or stationary traffic.

items.section: B · Traffic problems and road incidents
items.example: Congestion around the station has worsened since the roadworks began.
items.note: An accumulation of traffic that prevents it from moving freely.

items.pt: tarifa cobrada para circular em área congestionada
items.section: B · Traffic problems and road incidents
items.example: A congestion charge can discourage unnecessary journeys by car.
items.note: A fee for driving in a designated area, not an ordinary parking charge.

items.section: B · Traffic problems and road incidents
items.example: We had to pay a toll to use the bridge.
items.note: Toll is a fee for using a road, tunnel or bridge.

items.section: B · Traffic problems and road incidents
items.example: Dense fog caused a multi-vehicle pile-up early in the morning.
items.note: A crash involving several vehicles, often with successive impacts.

items.pt: ser desviado; ter a rota alterada
items.section: B · Traffic problems and road incidents
items.example: Traffic was diverted through nearby villages while the tunnel was closed.
items.note: Usually traffic is diverted onto or via another route.

items.section: B · Traffic problems and road incidents
items.example: Flooding caused major disruption to road and rail services.
items.note: Interference with normal transport or other operations.

items.pt: área sujeita a remoção de veículo estacionado irregularmente
items.section: B · Traffic problems and road incidents
items.example: The parking sign warned that the loading bay was a tow-away zone.
items.note: Vehicles may be removed by authorities if parked there unlawfully.

items.pt: imobilizar um carro com trava na roda
items.section: B · Traffic problems and road incidents
items.example: The enforcement company clamped the car after a parking violation.
items.note: British English: fit a wheel clamp; rules on clamping vary by jurisdiction.

items.pt: agressividade no trânsito; fúria ao volante
items.section: B · Traffic problems and road incidents
items.example: A minor disagreement escalated into an episode of road rage.
items.note: Extreme anger or aggression between motorists.

items.section: B · Traffic problems and road incidents
items.example: The car began to skid on the icy bend.
items.note: A vehicle slides and may lose traction or steering control.

items.section: B · Traffic problems and road incidents
items.example: Two vehicles were involved in a head-on collision on the narrow road.
items.note: A collision in which the fronts of vehicles hit one another.

items.section: B · Traffic problems and road incidents
items.example: We were stuck in traffic for nearly an hour.
items.note: An ordinary expression for being unable to move normally because of congestion.

items.pt: trânsito completamente parado; paralisação total do tráfego
items.section: Exercises · Additional motoring expressions
items.example: One broken traffic light created gridlock across several junctions.
items.note: A total standstill of traffic, stronger than ordinary congestion.

items.pt: encostar o veículo à beira da via
items.section: Exercises · Additional motoring expressions
items.example: The officer signalled for the driver to pull over safely.
items.note: Drive to the roadside and stop; a common phrasal verb.

items.section: Exercises · Additional motoring expressions
items.example: There was a minor bump in the supermarket car park.
items.note: Informal term for a small traffic collision, typically with limited damage.

items.pt: pifar; parar de funcionar de repente
items.section: Exercises · Additional motoring expressions
items.example: Our old car conked out halfway up the hill.
items.note: Very informal for a machine or vehicle suddenly stopping working.

items.pt: passageiro que fica dando palpites sobre como dirigir
items.section: Exercises · Additional motoring expressions
items.example: My brother becomes a back-seat driver whenever I take the wheel.
items.note: Figuratively a person who gives unwanted instructions, even when not in a car.

units.title: Unit 26 — Travel and accommodation
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 26. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
units.category: Travel and tourism · bookings, transport, accommodation and holiday idioms
learningObjectives: Distinguish scheduled and charter flights, ticket restrictions, transfers, fare classes and inclusive packages.
Describe sea and rail travel accurately, including crossings, cabins, berths, decks and through trains.
Compare holiday accommodation and board arrangements using British-English travel terminology.
Use idiomatic holiday expressions and collocations with an awareness of register and intended meaning.

sectionsChecked: All teaching-page text, vocabulary explanations and layout or illustration-based targets
Register, lexical contrasts, phrasal verbs and relevant usage patterns

items.section: A · Air travel, fares and bookings
items.example: We booked a scheduled flight rather than a special group charter.
items.note: A regular flight on an airline timetable; contrast with charter flight.

items.section: A · Air travel, fares and bookings
items.example: The travel company arranged a charter flight for the holidaymakers.
items.note: A flight specially organised for a particular group or tour operation.

items.section: A · Air travel, fares and bookings
items.example: Her employer approved first class for the long journey.
items.note: A high-service travel class; the details vary between carriers.

items.section: A · Air travel, fares and bookings
items.example: The airline upgraded the team to business class.
items.note: Travel class usually offering more comfort or flexibility than economy.

items.section: A · Air travel, fares and bookings
items.example: Most passengers on the route fly in economy class.
items.note: Often the least expensive standard travel class.

items.section: A · Air travel, fares and bookings
items.example: We flew via Lisbon before continuing to our destination.
items.note: Via introduces an intermediate route or connecting place, not necessarily a lengthy stopover.

items.section: A · Air travel, fares and bookings
items.example: A low-cost airline offered the cheapest base fare.
items.note: Budget airline; extra services may cost more.

items.pt: companhia aérea nacional; transportadora aérea de referência do país
items.section: A · Air travel, fares and bookings
items.example: The national carrier serves several regional airports.
items.note: A major airline associated with a country; not necessarily state-owned.

items.pt: somente passagem aérea; pacote apenas com voo
items.section: A · Air travel, fares and bookings
items.example: We chose a flight-only booking and arranged accommodation ourselves.
items.note: Travel product that excludes hotel accommodation and other holiday services.

items.section: A · Air travel, fares and bookings
items.example: The package holiday covered flights, a hotel and airport transfers.
items.note: Travel and accommodation sold together for an overall price.

items.section: A · Air travel, fares and bookings
items.example: They chose an all-inclusive holiday to simplify their budget.
items.note: Typically includes travel, lodging and meals, though what is included depends on the offer.

items.section: A · Air travel, fares and bookings
items.example: Check whether airport taxes are included in the fare.
items.note: Charges related to air travel; not identical to optional extras.

items.pt: serviços adicionais pagos à parte na viagem
items.section: A · Air travel, fares and bookings
items.example: Insurance and seat selection were sold as travel extras.
items.note: Additional products or services beyond the basic fare.

items.section: A · Air travel, fares and bookings
items.example: Read the ticket restrictions before choosing a cheap fare.
items.note: Rules limiting changes, dates, refunds or eligibility.

items.section: A · Air travel, fares and bookings
items.example: The early booking turned out to be good value for money.
items.note: A favourable balance between price and what you receive, not simply a low price.

items.section: A · Air travel, fares and bookings
items.example: The discounted fare was non-refundable after purchase.
items.note: Payment cannot normally be returned if cancelled; check terms.

items.section: A · Air travel, fares and bookings
items.example: We paid a cancellation fee when we changed our plans.
items.note: A charge for cancelling a reservation.

items.pt: parada intermediária com permanência antes de prosseguir a viagem
items.section: A · Air travel, fares and bookings
items.example: We arranged a two-night stopover in Singapore.
items.note: A planned break in a journey, often longer than a routine connection.

items.section: A · Air travel, fares and bookings
items.example: An airport transfer was included in the booking.
items.note: Transport between the airport and accommodation; the text uses plural transfers.

items.pt: ônibus de traslado; ônibus circular de conexão
items.section: A · Air travel, fares and bookings
items.example: A shuttle bus takes guests from the terminal to the hotel.
items.note: A bus providing repeated trips along a short route.

items.section: A · Sea travel and cruises
items.example: We took the ferry to the island early in the morning.
items.note: A boat that carries people and sometimes vehicles across water.

items.section: A · Sea travel and cruises
items.example: The crossing was calm despite the strong wind.
items.note: In this unit, the journey made by ferry across an area of water.

items.section: A · Sea travel and cruises
items.example: They booked a cruise along the coast of Norway.
items.note: A holiday travelling by ship, often calling at different ports.

items.section: A · Sea travel and cruises
items.example: A luxury cruise was beyond their usual holiday budget.
items.note: Cruise offering a high level of comfort, services and facilities.

items.section: A · Sea travel and cruises
items.example: For her parents, visiting Antarctica was the holiday of a lifetime.
items.note: An exceptional holiday expected to be remembered for years.

items.pt: beliche ou leito em navio ou trem
items.section: A · Sea travel and cruises
items.example: I reserved the upper berth in a four-person cabin.
items.note: A fixed bed or sleeping space on a boat or train.

items.section: A · Sea travel and cruises
items.example: A shared cabin costs less than a private suite.
items.note: Accommodation on a boat shared by more than one passenger or party.

items.pt: cabine de categoria superior; cabine de luxo
items.section: A · Sea travel and cruises
items.example: The deluxe cabin had a private balcony.
items.note: An upgraded cabin category, often marketed as more comfortable.

items.section: A · Sea travel and cruises
items.example: We watched the sunset from the upper deck.
items.note: A higher level of a boat or ship.

items.pt: ilhas exóticas; ilhas de paisagem pouco familiar
items.section: A · Sea travel and cruises
items.example: The travel agency advertised visits to exotic islands.
items.note: In promotional language, exotic suggests unusual or exciting to the target audience.

items.pt: fugir da rotina; afastar-se de tudo para descansar
items.section: A · Sea travel and cruises
items.example: They rented a cottage in the hills to get away from it all.
items.note: Idiomatic expression for escaping everyday pressures and routines.

items.section: A · Rail travel and car hire
items.example: Passengers moved into the next carriage when the air conditioning failed.
items.note: British English for a railway passenger coach.

items.section: A · Rail travel and car hire
items.example: You need to change trains at York to reach the village.
items.note: Leave one train and board another during a journey.

items.pt: trem direto, sem troca de composição
items.section: A · Rail travel and car hire
items.example: We found a through train and avoided changing at the junction.
items.note: A train that serves the destination without requiring a change; it may still make intermediate stops.

items.section: A · Rail travel and car hire
items.example: Car hire was more convenient than using buses in the countryside.
items.note: British English; American English usually says car rental.

items.pt: quilometragem livre; sem limite de distância
items.section: A · Rail travel and car hire
items.example: The agreement included unlimited mileage for the week.
items.note: The hire price does not increase with distance driven, subject to contract terms.

items.section: A · Rail travel and car hire
items.example: Check the accident insurance conditions before collecting the car.
items.note: Insurance cover associated with hired vehicles; coverage varies.

items.pt: circular; deslocar-se de um lugar a outro
items.section: A · Rail travel and car hire
items.example: Cycling is an easy way to get around the city.
items.note: Informal phrasal verb meaning travel between places locally.

items.word: come and go as you please
items.pt: ir e vir quando quiser; ter liberdade de horários
items.section: A · Rail travel and car hire
items.example: With a hire car, we could come and go as we pleased.
items.note: Emphasises flexibility and freedom from a fixed schedule.

items.section: B · Accommodation and meals
items.example: Camping in the mountains requires suitable equipment.
items.note: Staying in a tent or caravan rather than a conventional hotel.

items.pt: viagem com hospedagem sem refeições incluídas e cozinha própria
items.section: B · Accommodation and meals
items.example: We booked a self-catering holiday and shopped at local markets.
items.note: Guests prepare their own meals; contrasts with board options.

items.section: B · Accommodation and meals
items.example: The ski resort had a small wooden chalet near the slopes.
items.note: Holiday cottage or cabin, commonly found in mountain resorts.

items.section: B · Accommodation and meals
items.example: The guest house offered quiet rooms and homemade breakfasts.
items.note: A small lodging establishment, often less formal than a large hotel.

items.section: B · Accommodation and meals
items.example: We stayed at an old inn beside the village square.

items.pt: meia-pensão; café da manhã e mais uma refeição
items.section: B · Accommodation and meals
items.example: The hotel offered half board with breakfast and dinner.
items.note: Usually includes breakfast and one other meal; confirm the exact arrangement.

items.pt: pensão completa; hospedagem com três refeições
items.section: B · Accommodation and meals
items.example: Families can choose full board for an additional charge.
items.note: Typically includes breakfast, lunch and dinner; drinks may be excluded.

items.pt: acampar ou viajar sem conforto; passar perrengue
items.section: Exercises · Describing holiday experiences
items.example: We decided to rough it and camp without electricity for three days.

items.pt: continuar em movimento; não ficar muito tempo no mesmo lugar
items.section: Exercises · Describing holiday experiences

items.pt: dormir ao relento; dormir sob as estrelas
items.section: Exercises · Describing holiday experiences

items.section: Exercises · Describing holiday experiences

items.pt: estar em lugar remoto, longe da civilização
items.section: Exercises · Describing holiday experiences

items.section: Exercises · Describing holiday experiences
items.example: Meeting local conservationists was a real learning experience.

items.pt: ficar à toa; relaxar sem fazer muita coisa

items.section: Exercises · Describing holiday experiences
